title: Cartwise Shopper Batches Long-Distance Bonus Postings and the Pay-Component Posting Tool
content:
A long-distance bonus that is due on a completed batch of Cartwise Shopper Batches but absent from the batch's earnings entries is posted by the desk as one long-distance pay component, once per batch. Components are posted only on a batch that is completed or canceled, never on a dropped one.

## What the posting governs

| Point | Rule |
|---|---|
| Batch | A completed batch on which a long-distance bonus is due |
| Entry booked | One long-distance pay component among the batch's earnings entries |
| How often | Once per batch |
| Who posts it | The desk |
| Status the batch must hold | Completed or canceled, never dropped |

A batch whose earnings entries already carry a long-distance pay component has had its bonus posted; the posting is made once per batch.

## Situation of use and capability of `post_pay_component_6b97a1a8`

`post_pay_component_6b97a1a8` credits one pay component to a shopper batch on the shopper's behalf. One call books a single pay-component earnings entry on the named batch with today's posting date and raises the batch's earnings (the shopper's earnings on the batch including tips) by the same amount; the new entry and the raised earnings are visible at once in the batch's earnings entries and in the shopper's pay breakdown.

## How it is invoked

It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `post_pay_component_6b97a1a8` and then calls it.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `batch_id` | The batch number of the shopper batch being paid, as returned by the batch lookup for the verified shopper | Id |
| `pay_component` | Which pay component the entry credits | Enum, exactly one value from the list below |
| `order_id` | The order number the component belongs to for a per-order component, as returned by the order lookup for the batch; an empty string "" for a batch-level component, which belongs to no single order | Id, or "" |
| `amount_usd` | The amount credited, in USD | A positive number with 2 decimal places, already rounded to the cent by the caller; stored rounded to 2 decimal places |

Values of `pay_component`:

- `batch_base` — the fixed pay for completing the batch
- `per_order` — the pay for one order carried beyond the first
- `per_item` — the pay for the item units shopped
- `staging` — the pay for an order staged for pickup or handoff
- `mileage` — the pay for estimated route miles beyond the included miles
- `long_distance` — the bonus for an estimated route beyond the long-distance threshold
- `heavy_pay` — the pay for heavy units once heavy pay starts
- `wait_time` — the pay for recorded waiting beyond the unpaid minutes
- `peak_boost` — the boost shown on the accepted offer
- `quality_bonus` — the bonus for an order rated five stars in time with no item refund
- `return_pay` — the pay for an order returned to the store after the required contact attempts
- `minimum_topup` — the amount that lifts the batch's pay before tips to its minimum
- `cancellation_pay` — the pay for a batch whose every order was canceled after shopping started

## Return

A text receipt of a dictionary carrying `batch_event_id` (the reference number of the new earnings entry), `batch_id`, `pay_component`, `amount_usd` (USD, 2 decimal places), `event_date` (the posting date, YYYY-MM-DD) and `batch_earnings_usd` (the batch's earnings once the credit is booked, USD, 2 decimal places). Receiving the `batch_event_id` means the credit is booked. The tool computes no pay figure and checks no eligibility.
